'''''Schoenoplectus lacustris''''', the '''common club-rush''',<ref name="IUCN"/><ref name="PlantAtlas">{{cite web | title=Common Club-rush ''Schoenoplectus lacustris'' (L.) Palla | website=PlantAtlas | url=https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.1zk | access-date=2025-08-31}}</ref> is a species of club-rush (genus ''[[Schoenoplectus]]'') that grows in fresh water across Europe, much of Asia, and with a disjunct population in southern Africa.<ref name="POWO">{{cite web | title=''Schoenoplectus lacustris'' (L.) Palla | website=Plants of the World Online | date=2020-08-01 | url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:1019162-1 | access-date=2025-08-31}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:20180725Schoenoplectus lacustris3.jpg|thumb|left|The young flowerhead can resemble a club, whence the English name of the plant]]
''Schoenoplectus lacustris'' grows up to {{convert|3.5|m}} tall, with mid to dark green (not glaucous) stems {{cvt|5|-|15|mm|in|1}} thick.<ref name="Streeter">{{cite book | last=Streeter | first=David | title=Flower Guide | publisher=Collins | publication-place=London | date=2010 | isbn=978-0-00-718389-0 | page=554}}</ref><ref name="Jermy">{{cite book |author=A. C. Jermy |author2=D. A. Simpson |author3=M. J. Y. Foley |author4=M. S. Porter |name-list-style=amp |year=2007 |title=Sedges of the British Isles |series=BSBI Handbook |volume=1 |edition=3rd |publisher=[[Botanical Society of the British Isles]] |isbn=978-0-901158-35-2 |chapter=''Schoenoplectus lacustris'' (L.) Palla |pages=105–107}}</ref> Most of the leaves of ''S. lacustris'' are reduced to bladeless sheaths around the stem, but leaf blades up to {{cvt|100|cm|in|-1}} long can be formed under water.<ref name="Jermy"/> The [[inflorescence]] appears at the top of the stem, and comprises 3–10 branches, each of which is up to {{cvt|10|cm|in|0}} long and may be again divided into shorter branches. The [[flower]]s are in the form of [[spikelet]]s, each of which is {{cvt|6|-|15|mm|in|1}} long by {{convert|3|-|5|mm|in|1}} wide.<ref name="Jermy"/> It typically grows in water 0.3–⁠1.5 m deep, but can grow in water deeper than this.<ref name="PlantAtlas"/>

The stems are round in cross-section, in contrast to the triquetrous (rounded-triangular) stems of other species in the genus, such as ''[[Schoenoplectus triqueter|S. triqueter]]'' and ''[[Schoenoplectus pungens|S. pungens]]''.<ref name="Jermy"/><ref name="Kukkonen">{{cite journal |author=I. Kukkonen |year=1996 |title=Notes on the treatment of Cyperaceae for Flora Iranica |url=http://www.landesmuseum.at/pdf_frei_remote/ANNA_98BS_0087-0095.pdf |journal=Annalen des Naturhistorischen Museums in Wien |volume=98BS |pages=87–95}}</ref> The stems of ''[[Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani|S. tabernaemontani]]'' (grey club-rush) are also round, but ''S. tabernaemontani'' is a smaller plant, less than {{convert|1.5|m|ft|abbr=on|frac=2}} tall, with only two stigmas per flower, and has glaucous grey-green stems.<ref name="Streeter"/><ref name="Jermy"/>

==Distribution==
''Schoenoplectus lacustris'' is widespread in Europe, albeit rare in the far north,<ref name="nrm">{{cite web |url=http://linnaeus.nrm.se/flora/mono/cypera/schoe/scholac.html |title=Säv, ''Schoenoplectus lacustris'' (L.) Palla |work=Den Virtuella Floran |language=Swedish |publisher=[[Swedish Museum of Natural History|Naturhistoriska Riksmuseet]] |date=28 October 2005 |accessdate=1 April 2015}}</ref> and extends eastwards into Asia as far as [[Mongolia]].<ref name="eMonocot">{{cite web |url=http://e-monocot.org/taxon/urn:kew.org:wcs:taxon:262997 |title=''Schoenoplectus lacustris'' (L.) Palla |publisher=[[eMonocot]] |accessdate=1 April 2015 |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142503/http://e-monocot.org/taxon/urn:kew.org:wcs:taxon:262997 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It is also found in a number of Mediterranean sites in North Africa,<ref name="nrm"/> and has been [[introduced species|introduced]] to Bangladesh and Haiti.<ref name="POWO"/>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] as ''Scirpus lacustris'' in his 1753 ''{{lang|la|[[Species Plantarum]]}}''. It became part of the genus ''[[Schoenoplectus]]'' when [[Eduard Palla]] raised this from the rank of subgenus to the rank of genus in 1888.<ref name="eMonocot"/><ref>{{cite journal |author=Eduard Palla |author-link=Eduard Palla |year=1888 |title=Im botanischen Discussionsabende am 16. März sprach Herr Dr. Ed. Palla ber die Gattung ''Scirpus'' |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/47683#page/111/mode/1up |journal=Verhandlungen des Kaiserlich-königlichen Zoologisch-botanischen Gesellschaft in Wien |volume=38 |page=49}}</ref> Two subspecies are recognised; the [[Autonym (botany)|autonymic]] subspecies (''S. lacustris'' subsp. ''lacustris'') is found throughout the range of the species, and a second, ''S. lacustris'' subsp. ''hippolyti'' is restricted to an area reaching from the [[Caucasus]] to the mountains of Central Asia.<ref name="POWO"/> It can [[Hybrid (biology)|hybridise]] with ''S. tabernaemontani'', the hybrid being known as ''Schoenoplectus × flevensis''; this hybrid is known from Great Britain, the Netherlands, Germany, and the Baltic States.<ref>{{cite web | title=''Schoenoplectus × flevensis'' (D.Bakker) Lansdown & Rumsey | website=Plants of the World Online | url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77214823-1 | access-date=2025-08-31}}</ref>
